definition: Multi-fidelity Optimization uses cheap, lower-fidelity evaluations, such as fewer epochs or fewer data points, to allocate computation toward promising configurations before spending the full budget.
intuition: Use cheap imperfect signals to eliminate weak trials early; reserve full training budgets for candidates that survive.
mathematical_foundation:
$$
c(\lambda, r), \quad r \in \mathcal{R}
$$

`r` is a resource or fidelity level, such as epochs, data volume, or resolution. Low `r` gives a cheaper but noisier estimate of final cost.
advantages: Can trade fidelity bias against much lower evaluation cost.
Converts partial learning-curve information into search savings.
Rejects weak configurations before full training.
limitations: Low-fidelity performance may not rank configurations reliably at full budget.
The method needs a meaningful resource axis and a useful early signal.
